jobs.title: Creative Content Creator
jobs.description:
yasma natura membuka lowongan untuk posisi creative content creator. pekerjaan melibatkan pembuatan ide, konsep, serta script konten media sosial, penyuntingan video hingga siap rilis, dan pengelolaan konten tiktok serta instagram. kandidat juga bertugas mengikuti tren short video, berkoordinasi terkait seo, meta, dan ai generative untuk digital marketing, mendokumentasikan aktivitas perusahaan, serta mengevaluasi performa konten. benefit mencakup gaji pokok, tunjangan, bpjstk, asuransi, dan jenjang karir.

kandidat minimal lulusan sma/smk sederajat, pria/wanita usia 19-27 tahun. mampu membuat konsep, script, shooting, serta editing video (capcut/vn/adobe premiere). memahami tiktok, instagram reels, dan tren konten video pendek. memiliki portofolio konten menjadi nilai tambah. diutamakan berdomisili sidoarjo.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi middle mile supervisor di spx express bertugas memantau dan memimpin operasional middle mile dari 3pl/in house di kab. maros, sulawesi selatan. tanggung jawab meliputi berkolaborasi dengan tim lm, mm, dan fm terkait lead time, durasi delivery, dan kebutuhan trip. selain itu, posisi ini berkoordinasi dengan tim fleet untuk memastikan kesiapan unit, melakukan pemetaan rute, memaksimalkan penggunaan unit, serta mengalokasikan perencanaan sumber daya untuk implementasi baru distribution center (dc).

pendidikan minimal sma/diploma dari semua jurusan. memiliki pengalaman kerja 3-5 tahun di industri transportasi, logistik, atau rantai pasokan. memiliki pengalaman dalam menangani operasi darat, udara, maupun laut. mahir menggunakan microsoft office dan memiliki keterampilan komunikasi yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shifting serta bersedia ditempatkan di area yang ditentukan.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Coordinator Air & Sea
jobs.description:
bertanggung jawab melakukan koordinasi dan pengawasan langsung terhadap proses inbound dan outbound di area warehouse dc, bandara (air freight), dan pelabuhan (sea freight). memastikan kelengkapan serta kesesuaian dokumen unit armada vendor yang melakukan pickup, memantau jadwal keberangkatan dan kedatangan unit armada agar serah terima barang tepat waktu sesuai sla, serta memperbarui data pergerakan paket secara real-time ke pemangku kepentingan terkait.

pendidikan minimal sma atau diploma. mampu mengoperasikan microsoft excel dengan baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem kerja shift. bersedia bekerja di area bandara atau pelabuhan. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi yang baik.

jobs.title: Middle Mile Coordinator
jobs.description:
bertanggung jawab untuk memantau proses masuk dan keluarnya barang hingga diproses ke linehaul, serta memastikan alur penyortiran barang berjalan sesuai dengan standard operating procedure (sop). merencanakan kebutuhan tenaga kerja berdasarkan fluktuasi volume harian, memantau produktivitas, kapasitas, dan kesiapan peralatan di sortation center. melakukan briefing rutin bersama tim operasional terkait laporan kerja harian dan penerapan budaya kerja 5s.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat atau lebih tinggi. memiliki pengalaman kerja minimal 1 tahun sebagai staf transportasi di bidang logistik atau transportasi. mampu mengoperasikan microsoft excel secara mahir, khususnya rumus vlookup dan sumif. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi interpersonal yang baik. bersedia bekerja dengan sistem shift dan siap ditempatkan di area banjarmasin dc, kabupaten banjar, kalimantan selatan.

jobs.title: Driver Management Supervisor
jobs.description:
posisi driver management supervisor bertanggung jawab untuk melakukan evaluasi kehadiran driver sesuai jadwal yang ditetapkan, mengelola pelatihan, penilaian kinerja, serta peningkatan kompetensi driver secara berkala. selain itu, posisi ini bertugas melakukan pembinaan dan berkoordinasi dengan tim hse guna mencegah kecelakaan kerja, proaktif melakukan pemecahan masalah untuk perbaikan kinerja beserta efektivitasnya, serta bertanggung jawab atas pencapaian target dari kinerja dan pengembangan tim di penempatan banjarmasin dc, kab. banjar.

pendidikan minimal d3 semua jurusan, namun diutamakan dari jurusan logistik atau supply chain. memiliki pengalaman 3-5 tahun di bidang logistik/ekspres dan driver management. memiliki skill teknis manajemen armada & roster serta memahami standar k3/hse. memiliki kemampuan problem solving, komunikasi, dan kepemimpinan.

jobs.title: Sortation Center Shift Lead
jobs.description:
posisi sortation center shift lead bertanggung jawab memantau operasional harian sortation center (soc) mencakup pengawasan proses inbound, sortation, bagging, reprocessing, hingga outbound. memastikan seluruh fungsi operasional berjalan sesuai standard operating procedure (sop), merencanakan kebutuhan tenaga kerja berdasarkan fluktuasi volume harian, serta memantau produktivitas, kapasitas, dan peralatan kerja. bertanggung jawab juga dalam memimpin briefing berkala dengan tim terkait laporan kerja dan implementasi budaya kerja 5s (sort, set in order, shine, standardize, sustain). penempatan di kab. maros, sulawesi selatan.

pendidikan minimal sma/smk sederajat atau lebih tinggi. memiliki pengalaman kerja 2-3 tahun di bidang logistik, pergudangan, atau sejenis sebagai kepala gudang atau supervisor. memiliki kemampuan komunikasi dan kepemimpinan yang baik. bersedia bekerja dalam sistem shift serta siap ditempatkan di lokasi kerja yang ditentukan.

jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humani aria cuyo manda o es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en si uación de vulnerabilidad. jobs.title: Étude sur l’architecture de la première réponse d’urgence au mali : capacités existantes, contraintes et perspectives d’évolution
jobs.description:
**1. Con ex e e jus ifica ion**

Le Mali fai face à une crise humani aire e sécuri aire prolongée, carac érisée par des déplacemen s de popula ions, des confli s e violences, des res ric ions d’accès, des chocs clima iques e d’impor an s besoins humani aires. Dans ce con ex e, la capaci é à me re en place une réponse rapide e appropriée immédia emen après un choc cons i ue un élémen essen iel d’une ac ion humani aire efficace.

Ces dernières années, les mécanismes de réponse d’urgence on cons i ué l’un des principaux disposi ifs perme an de répondre rapidemen aux besoins urgen s des popula ions affec ées par de nouveaux chocs. Tou efois, l’évolu ion du con ex e malien, les con rain es d’accès, le financemen humani aire, le renforcemen des capaci és des ac eurs na ionaux e locaux ainsi que l’agenda de localisa ion posen la ques ion de l’archi ec ure fu ure de la première réponse d’urgence.

Il es donc nécessaire de mieux comprendre quels ac eurs son ac uellemen en mesure d’assurer les différen es fonc ions de la première réponse, dans quelles condi ions e avec quelles limi es, ainsi que les améliora ions possibles. À la sui e d’un choc, commen la première réponse d’urgence devrai -elle ê re organisée au Mali, quels ac eurs son les mieux placés pour assurer chacune des fonc ions essen ielles, commen peuven -ils se complé er, e quelles archi ec ures son réalis es selon les différen s con ex es ?

L’é ude vise ainsi à éclairer les choix fu urs en iden ifian des modèles de réponse d’urgence rapides, efficaces, réalis es, complémen aires e adap és à la diversi é des con ex es maliens, plu ô que de se limi er à proposer des ajus emen s au mécanisme exis an .

Dans ce con ex e, l’é ude ne vise pas uniquemen à dé erminer commen renforcer ou in égrer les capaci és locales dans les mécanismes exis an s de réponse d’urgence. Plus largemen , elle vise à dé erminer quelle archi ec ure de première réponse d’urgence es la mieux adap ée aux con ex es ac uels du Mali, en enan comp e des capaci és déjà disponibles aux niveaux é a ique, local, communau aire e humani aire, ainsi que des con rain es opéra ionnelles e financières qui influencen leur mobilisa ion.

L’é ude sera donc s ruc urée au our des fonc ions essen ielles de la première réponse d’urgence, plu ô qu’au our d’une analyse ins i u ionnelle générale. Elle cherchera à comprendre quels ac eurs son ac uellemen en mesure d’exercer ces fonc ions, dans quelles circons ances, avec quelles limi es, e commen leurs rôles pourraien ê re organisés de manière plus complémen aire.

Ce e approche devrai abou ir à plusieurs modèles ou scénarios opéra ionnels adap és aux différen s con ex es maliens, plu ô qu’à une recommanda ion unique applicable à l’ensemble du pays.

**2. Objec if de l’é ude**

L’objec if de ce e é ude es d’analyser commen la première réponse d’urgence à la sui e d’un choc devrai ê re organisée au Mali, en iden ifian :

- les capaci és humaines, financières, ma érielles e de pres a ion de services exis an es des différen s ac eurs concernés ;
- les fonc ions essen ielles de la première réponse e les ac eurs capables de les assurer efficacemen ;
- les fac eurs qui facili en ou limi en leur mobilisa ion ;
- les complémen ari és e les éven uels chevauchemen s en re ac eurs ;
- les fonc ions pour lesquelles le leadership des ac eurs humani aires demeure nécessaire ;
- les fonc ions qui pourraien progressivemen ê re par agées avec ou assurées par des ac eurs é a iques, locaux ou communau aires ;
- e les modèles de première réponse les plus per inen s selon les différen s con ex es.

L’é ude devra donc produire des conclusions opéra ionnelles pouvan ê re direc emen u ilisées pour concevoir ou faire évoluer les fu urs mécanismes de réponse d’urgence au Mali.

**3. Périmè re de l’é ude**

Le périmè re cons i ue un élémen cen ral de ce e é ude afin d’évi er que l’analyse ne s’é ende à une évalua ion générale du sys ème humani aire malien.

**3.1. Périmè re héma ique**

L'é ude se concen re exclusivemen sur l'organisa ion de la première phase de la réponse faisan sui e à un choc.

Elle analysera no ammen les fonc ions suivan es:

1. Aler e e iden ifica ion du choc
2. Vérifica ion e analyse rapide de la si ua ion
3. Enregis remen e iden ifica ion des popula ions affec ées
4. Ciblage e priorisa ion des besoins
5. Mobilisa ion e coordina ion de la première réponse
6. Fourni ure ou facili a ion de l’assis ance de première ligne
7. Référencemen vers les services e mécanismes de réponse appropriés
8. Informa ion, communica ion communau aire e redevabili é
9. Suivi de la réponse ini iale e adap a ion de celle-ci

L’analyse por era sur la manière don ces fonc ions son ac uellemen assurées, les ac eurs qui les exercen , leurs capaci és e leurs limi es, ainsi que les possibili és réalis es d’organisa ion fu ure.

L’é ude examinera égalemen les condi ions nécessaires pour assurer la con inui é en re la première réponse e les mécanismes de réponse ul érieurs, sans ou efois procéder à une analyse dé aillée des phases suivan es de la réponse humani aire.

**3.2. Défini ion de la « première réponse d’urgence »**

Aux fins de ce e é ude, la première réponse d’urgence désigne la période immédia emen consécu ive à un choc duran laquelle les ac eurs doiven :

- iden ifier e vérifier le choc ;
- comprendre rapidemen son ampleur e ses conséquences ;
- iden ifier les popula ions affec ées e leurs besoins priori aires ;
- mobiliser les ac eurs e les ressources disponibles ;
- fournir ou facili er une assis ance urgen e ;
- orien er les personnes vers les services e mécanismes appropriés ;
- assurer un suivi ini ial afin d’adap er la réponse.

La durée exac e de ce e première phase pourra varier selon la na ure e l’ampleur du choc e sera convenue avec le consul an lors de la phase de démarrage. Tou efois, l’analyse devra res er cen rée sur la réponse ini iale e non sur l’ensemble du cycle de réponse humani aire.

**3.3. Types de chocs considérés**

L’é ude pourra prendre en comp e différen s ypes de chocs suscep ibles de déclencher une réponse rapide, no ammen :

- les confli s e violences ;
- les déplacemen s soudains de popula ions ;
- les ca as rophes ou chocs na urels ;
- d’au res événemen s en raînan une dé ériora ion soudaine e significa ive des condi ions de vie ou de la pro ec ion de la popula ion.

L’objec if n’es pas de réaliser une analyse sec orielle de chaque ype de crise, mais d’iden ifier dans quelle mesure l’archi ec ure de la première réponse devrai varier selon la na ure du choc.

**3.4. Ac eurs couver s**

L’é ude analysera uniquemen les ac eurs qui jouen , ou pourraien de manière réalis e jouer, un rôle dans la première réponse d’urgence.

**a) Ac eurs é a iques**

- s ruc ures de l’É a aux niveaux na ional, régional e local ;
- au ori és adminis ra ives e echniques compé en es ;
- s ruc ures publiques pouvan con ribuer à l’aler e, à l’évalua ion, à la coordina ion, à l’orien a ion ou à la réponse ini iale.

**b) S ruc ures communau aires e ac eurs locaux**

- au ori és e s ruc ures communau aires ;
- ac eurs cou umiers e religieux ;
- organisa ions e associa ions locales ;
- groupes communau aires per inen s ;
- familles e communau és d’accueil ;
- ac eurs privés lorsque leur con ribu ion à la première réponse es per inen e.

**c) Ac eurs humani aires**

- ONG na ionales e in erna ionales ;
- agences des Na ions Unies ;
- mécanismes de coordina ion e ac eurs impliqués dans la réponse rapide ;
- Au res ac eurs humani aires direc emen concernés par la première réponse.

d * *) Ac eurs du développemen * *

- Ac eurs du développemen uniquemen dans la mesure où leurs capaci és, ressources ou manda s peuven con ribuer à la première réponse ou à la ransi ion des fonc ions de réponse.

L’é ude ne cherchera donc pas à analyser l’ensemble du sys ème de développemen au Mali.

**NB :** Le rôle de l’É a sera analysé explici emen . Plu ô que de considérer le gouvernemen comme un ac eur parmi d’au res, l’é ude évaluera ses capaci és ac uelles, iden ifiera les fonc ions de réponse d’urgence qu’il assure déjà efficacemen , les lacunes persis an es, les domaines dans lesquels ces capaci és peuven ê re renforcées de manière réalis e au fil du emps, ainsi que les fonc ions pour lesquelles les ac eurs communau aires, locaux e humani aires con inueron d’appor er une réelle valeur ajou ée.

**4. Élémen s explici emen hors du périmè re**

Afin de préserver le carac ère opéra ionnel de l’é ude, les élémen s suivan s ne feron pas l’obje d’une analyse approfondie :

**4.1. Le sys ème humani aire dans son ensemble**

L’é ude ne vise pas à car ographier ni à évaluer l’ensemble des ins i u ions, organisa ions e mécanismes humani aires présen s au Mali. Les ac eurs seron analysés uniquemen au regard de leur rôle ac uel ou po en iel dans la première réponse d’urgence.

**4.2. L’ensemble du cycle humani aire**

L’é ude ne cons i ue pas une évalua ion de l’ensemble de la réponse humani aire, depuis la phase d’urgence jusqu’au relèvemen , au développemen ou aux solu ions durables. Les phases ul érieures ne seron abordées que lorsqu’elles on un impac direc sur l’organisa ion de la première réponse.

**4.3. Une évalua ion générale des capaci és ins i u ionnelles**

L’é ude ne réalisera pas une évalua ion ins i u ionnelle exhaus ive de l’É a , des communau és ou des ONG. Elle cherchera uniquemen à dé erminer quelles capaci és son effec ivemen disponibles e mobilisées pour les fonc ions de première réponse, dans quelles condi ions e avec quelles limi es.

**4.4. Une évalua ion exhaus ive du financemen humani aire**

Le financemen sera analysé comme un fac eur facili an ou con raignan l’organisa ion de la première réponse. L’é ude ne cherchera pas à réaliser une analyse exhaus ive des flux financiers humani aires au Mali ni une car ographie complè e du financemen des différen s sec eurs.

**4.5. Une réforme ins i u ionnelle générale**

L’é ude pourra formuler des recommanda ions ins i u ionnelles lorsque cela es nécessaire pour améliorer la première réponse, mais elle ne proposera pas de réforme générale de l’archi ec ure ins i u ionnelle de l’ac ion humani aire au Mali.

**5. Ques ion générale de recherche**

À la sui e d’un choc, commen la première réponse devrai -elle ê re organisée au Mali comp e enu des capaci és ac uelles, des avan ages compara ifs e des inci a ions des ac eurs é a iques, locaux/communau aires e humani aires, e quelles archi ec ures réalis es e complémen aires seraien les mieux adap ées aux différen s con ex es maliens ?

**6. Ques ions spécifiques de recherche**

**QR1. Car ographie des capaci és e fonc ions de réponse d’urgence**

Quelles son les capaci és ac uelles de l’É a , des s ruc ures communau aires, des ac eurs locaux e des ac eurs humani aires dans l’exercice des fonc ions clés de la réponse d’urgence au Mali ?

jobs.description:
## هدف الوظيفة

يحدد هذا الوصف مسؤولية مدير المشروع عن إدارة دورة المشروع كاملة، وتحقيق النتائج ضمن النطاق والميزانية والجدول المعتمد، مع ضمان جودة البناء وسلامة الأسر ووضوح حقوق الإشغال.

يقود مدير المشروع فريق التنفيذ وينسق مع الوزارة والسلطات ومقدمي الخدمات والأقسام المساندة في وطن لضمان تسليم مساكن آمنة وقابلة للإشغال

. ويتابع إحالة الأسر إلى خدمات التعليم والصحة والحماية وسبل العيش؛ وتبقى المساعدات التكميلية مرتبطة بالتزامات الشركاء وتوافر التمويل

## المهام والمسؤوليات

## إدارة المشروع والتخطيط

- إعداد خطة تنفيذ تفصيلية تربط المخرجات والأنشطة والجدول والموازنة والمسؤوليات؛ وتحديث الخطط الشهرية والأسبوعية ومتابعة المسار الحرج
- قيادة مراحل تأكيد المواقع والاتفاقيات، التصميم والاعتماد، المشتريات والتحقق من الأسر، البناء والخدمات، التسليم، والمتابعة وإصلاح العيوب
- إدارة نطاق المشروع والتغييرات وتأخر الأنشطة؛ واقتراح إجراءات تصحيحية ورفع التغييرات التي تتطلب موافقات إدارية أو موافقة المانح قبل تنفيذها
- توزيع مهام الفريق وتحديد أهداف الأداء والإشراف على الموظفين وتقييمهم، وتنظيم اجتماعات تقدم منتظمة مع المهندسين والمقاولين والأقسام المساندة
 
 ## تأكيد المواقع والتنسيق الحكومي
- •متابعة توثيق تخصيص الأرض وصلاحية استخدامها والاتفاقيات اللازمة مع الوزارة والجهات المختصة قبل بدء الإنشاء
- قيادة تقييم المواقع بالتعاون مع المختصين، بما يشمل السلامة وظروف التربة والمخاطر وإمكانات الربط بالخدمات والوصول الميسر إلى المدارس والصحة والأسواق والنقل.
- تنسيق إعداد واعتماد التصاميم والمواصفات وجداول الكميات والتراخيص مع مهندسي الوزارة وفريق وطن، وفق المتطلبات الفنية السورية المعتمدة

• استكمال مراجعة ترتيبات الإشغال مع الجهات المختصة والمشورة القانونية؛ وتوثيق الحقوق والمدة والتكاليف والمسؤوليات وآلية تسوية النزاعات قبل انتقال الأسر

## إدارة الإنشاء والجودة والسلامة

• اعتماد خطة متابعة الجودة ضمن الصلاحيات ومتابعة تطبيقها بواسطة المهندسين المؤهلين، بما يشمل فحص المواد والاختبارات ونقاط قبول الأعمال قبل إخفائها

• متابعة أداء المقاولين ونسب الإنجاز مقارنة بالعقود والخطة، والتحقق من معالجة الأعمال غير المطابقة وحفظ سجلات الفحوصات والزيارات وقرارات التصحيح

• ضمان تطبيق اشتراطات السلامة المهنية وحماية الأسر والمجتمعات المحيطة، ورفع الحوادث فوراً حسب الإجراءات؛ وتعليق الأعمال المتأثرة عند وجود خطر وشيك بالتنسيق مع الجهات المسؤولة

• عند الاشتباه بمخلفات متفجرة، إيقاف الأعمال في المنطقة المتأثرة وإحالة الأمر إلى الجهات المؤهلة؛ وعدم استئنافها قبل تأكيد السلامة

• متابعة اكتمال وربط واختبار المياه والصرف الصحي والكهرباء والتصريف والوصول الآمن؛ وعدم التوصية بإشغال أي وحدة قبل إثبات جاهزيتها ومعالجة العيوب الأساسية

## إدارة الميزانية والمشتريات والعقود

• إدارة الموازنة بالتنسيق مع المالية، ومراجعة المصروفات والالتزامات والتوقعات والتدفقات النقدية شهرياً، وتفسير الانحرافات واقتراح التصحيح

• إعداد خطة مشتريات مرتبطة بالجدول، وتنسيق الوثائق الفنية والطلبات والتقييم الفني مع الهندسة والمشتريات، وفق المنافسة والشفافية وسياسات وطن ومتطلبات المانح.

• متابعة تنفيذ العقود والتأخيرات والضمانات والاحتجازات والأوامر التغييرية، ضمن الصلاحيات والإجراءات المعتمدة

• مراجعة طلبات الدفع على أساس كميات وأعمال تحقّق منها المهندسون والوثائق التعاقدية؛ ورفعها للاعتماد المالي دون تجاوز الفصل بين الطلب والتحقق والاعتماد والصرف

## المهام والمسؤوليات متابعة

## اختيار الأسر والحماية والمساءلة

• تنسيق خطة التحقق من السجلات الحكومية مع فريق MEAL، وضمان تحقق مستقل من 100% من الأسر المقترحة قبل اعتماد قائمة المستفيدين وفق آلية الموافقة المعتمدة.

• توفير الموارد والوقت اللازمين لمعالجة التناقضات والتحقق من الأهلية ومنع الازدواجية؛ وصون استقلال نتائج MEAL وعدم تجاوزها أو تعديلها دون أدلة وإجراءات موثقة.

• الحفاظ على سرية الاختيار وعدم إجراء إعلان عام أو فتح باب تقديم خلال التحقق والاختيار، مع إبلاغ الأسر فردياً بأن التقييم لا يمثل وعداً بالمساعدة.

• ضمان الموافقة المستنيرة على جمع البيانات والمشاركة والانتقال، وشرح الموقع والخدمات وحقوق الإشغال والتكاليف المتوقعة بلغة مفهومة.

• ضمان قنوات شكاوى آمنة وسرية وميسرة، ومتابعة الشكاوى المتعلقة بالمشروع مع MEAL؛ وإحالة قضايا الحماية وحماية الطفل ومنع الاستغلال والانتهاك الجنسي وفق مسارات وطن المختصة.

• حماية بيانات الأسر وقصر الوصول عليها على المخولين؛ وعدم استخدام صور الأطفال أو بيانات الأسر في التقارير أو التواصل دون الموافقات والإجراءات اللازمة

## الشراكات والتقارير وإدارة المخاطر

• إدارة التنسيق التشغيلي مع HCI والوزارة والسلطات ومقدمي الخدمات، وتمثيل المشروع ضمن التفويض، وحفظ محاضر الاجتماعات والقرارات والالتزامات.

• تحديث سجل المخاطر والإجراءات والمسؤوليات؛ ومتابعة مخاطر الأرض والإشغال والتراخيص والتضخم والطقس وأداء المقاولين وتأخر الخدمات والتوترات المجتمعية.

• إعداد تقارير داخلية شهرية وتقارير المانح وفق الاتفاقية، تشمل الإنجاز الفعلي والمالي والجودة والأسر والمخاطر والإجراءات التصحيحية، بالتنسيق مع المالية وMEAL.

• تنسيق الإحالات والاتفاقات مع شركاء التعليم والصحة والحماية وسبل العيش، وتوثيق الالتزامات المؤكدة؛ وعدم تقديم وعود بمساعدات غير ممولة أو إدخال نشاط إضافي دون الاعتماد اللازم

## التسليم والمتابعة وإغلاق المشروع

• تنسيق فحص جميع الوحدات والخدمات، وقوائم العيوب ومعالجتها، ومحاضر الاستلام ووثائق الإشغال والتسليم الطوعي للأسر.

• الاتفاق على إدارة وصيانة المساحات والخدمات المشتركة وتكاليفها مع الجهات المعنية والسكان، وتوفير إرشادات الاستخدام الآمن والإبلاغ عن الأعطال.

• تنفيذ متابعة ما بعد الإشغال مع MEAL والهندسة، بما يشمل استمرار الإقامة والوصول إلى الخدمات والرضا والشكاوى وإصلاح العيوب خلال المدة التعاقدية.

• استكمال ملفات المشروع الفنية والمالية والتعاقدية ووثائق التنفيذ النهائي والاختبارات والضمانات، وإعداد التقرير الختامي والدروس المستفادة وخطة تسليم أي التزامات متبقية

## حدود الصلاحيات والمساءلة

يدير شاغل الوظيفة التنفيذ اليومي ويوجه الفريق ويتابع المقاولين ضمن التفويض المعتمد. تبقى المصادقة الفنية والتوقيع على الأعمال من اختصاص المهندسين المخولين، وتبقى الموافقات المالية والتعاقدية والاختيار النهائي للأسر وفق مصفوفة صلاحيات وطن. لا يلتزم المدير بتغيير جوهري في النطاق أو الموازنة أو المدة، أو بحقوق إشغال، أو بتمويل إضافي دون الموافقات المختصة. تُرفع العوائق والقرارات التي تتجاوز صلاحياته إلى مدير المشاريع في الوقت المناسب

## المخرجات المتوقعة ومعايير الأداء

• خطة بدء وتنفيذ متكاملة وجدول وموازنة وخطة مشتريات ومصفوفة مسؤوليات وسجل مخاطر، خلال الشهر الأول من المباشرة وتُحدّث دورياً

• ملف جاهزية لكل موقع قبل الإنشاء يتضمن تخصيص الأرض والاتفاقيات والتقييمات والتصاميم والكميات والتراخيص ومسؤوليات الخدمات

• تقارير تقدم شهرية موثقة تربط الإنجاز المادي بالمصروفات والالتزامات، مع متابعة الانحرافات والإجراءات التصحيحية؛ وتقارير مانح في مواعيدها

• قائمة 100 أسرة معتمدة بعد تحقق MEAL المستقل من جميع الأسر المقترحة، وحل التناقضات وتوثيق موافقتها المستنيرة وسرية بياناتها

• تسليم 100 وحدة ضمن النطاق والميزانية والجدول المعتمدين، مع سجلات فحص لكل وحدة، وخدمات أساسية عاملة وحقوق إشغال موثقة قبل الانتقال

• ملف تسليم وإغلاق يتضمن محاضر الاستلام، والاختبارات، والضمانات، وخطة الصيانة والمتابعة وسجل العيوب ومعالجتها والتقرير النهائي

## المؤهلات والخبرة المطلوبة

• بكالوريوس في الهندسة المدنية أو العمارة؛ وتُعد الدراسات العليا ذات الصلة أو شهادات إدارة المشاريع ميزة إضافية

• خبرة عملية لا تقل عن 7 سنوات في مشاريع الإنشاء أو الإسكان أو المأوى، منها 3 سنوات على الأقل في إدارة مشاريع تشمل فرقاً وميزانيات ومقاولين

• خبرة مثبتة في إدارة دورة مشروع ممول من مانح، والتخطيط والموازنة والمشتريات والعقود والتقارير؛ وخبرة البناء الدائم وربط البنية التحتية مطلوبة

• القدرة على مراجعة التصاميم والمواصفات وجداول الكميات وبرامج التنفيذ والمستخلصات، وإدارة الجودة والسلامة بالتعاون مع المختصين

• معرفة بالسياق السوري والعمل مع السلطات ومقدمي الخدمات والمجتمعات النازحة؛ وفهم مسائل حقوق الإشغال والحماية والمساءلة وحماية البيانات

• إتقان العربية، ومستوى مهني في الإنجليزية يسمح بإعداد التقارير والتواصل مع الشركاء.

• إجادة Excel وWord وبرامج الجدولة مثل MS Projec أو ما يعادلها، والقدرة على قراءة المخططات واستخدام أدوات متابعة الإنشاء؛ ويُفضل الإلمام بـ Au oCAD.

• القدرة على السفر المنتظم إلى مواقع المشروع ادلب والعمل ميدانياً وفق ترتيبات الأمن والسلامة

## المهارات والالتزامات المهنية

قيادة الفرق والتفاوض وحل المشكلات واتخاذ القرارات المبنية على الأدلة، وتنظيم الأولويات والتواصل مع الأطراف المختلفة، والنزاهة وإدارة تضارب المصالح. يلتزم شاغل الوظيفة بمدونة السلوك وسياسات وطن وإجراءاتها، والمبادئ الإنسانية وعدم التمييز، وحماية الطفل ومنع الاستغلال والانتهاك الجنسي ومكافحة الاحتيال، والإبلاغ عن المخالفات عبر القنوات المعتمدة.

- القدرة على العمل باستقلالية، وإدارة الأولويات، وإنجاز المهام بأقل قدر من الإشراف.
- الالتزام بأعلى معايير المهنية والنزاهة والسرية واحترام مبادئ حقوق الإنسان.
- اللغات:

 - إتقان ممتاز للغة الإنجليزية، تحدثًا وكتابةً.

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Blue Economy Investment Specialist, IPSA11, Fiji - Suva (UNCDF)- [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

  • Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
  • Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
  • Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
  • Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector.  By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders.  UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:  

  • SME Finance
  • Sub-National Finance
  • Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

UNCDF is seeking a Blue Economy Investment Specialist to lead the origination, structuring, and deployment of ocean-positive and nature-based blended finance investments in the Pacific. The position will focus on mobilizing concessional and catalytic capital toward enterprises and financial intermediaries that generate sustainable livelihoods while protecting and restoring coastal and marine ecosystems, with a particular emphasis on reef-positive, fisheries, aquaculture, coastal tourism, waste management, and ocean-climate resilience solutions.  

Among other tasks, the incumbent is expected to manage the blue economy portfolio in the Pacific, in particular the EU-funded Sustainable Pacific Blue Circle Fund (SPBCF) project, an impact investment vehicle that provides investment capital backed by venture-building support (technical assistance, grants, loans, guarantees) to businesses that have the potential to generate revenue and create a positive development impact ongoing till 2028. The incumbent is also expected to oversee other blue economy focused and reef-positive interventions that are implemented in the Pacific region. 

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Regional Investment Specialists for the Pacific and in close collaboration with other colleagues in IID and IFOD, the Blue Economy Investment Specialist will lead and support the development, structuring and execution of blue‑economy or other relevant sectoral investment initiatives.  The Specialist will work closely with IID and IFOD colleagues, as well as other UNCDF counterparts, country focal points, government partners, private sector actors and development partners.

1) Project Management of Blue‑Economy Investment Initiatives

  • Manage all aspects of the blue economy initiatives implemented in the Pacific.
  • Lead the preparation and implementation of Annual Work Plans (AWPs), budgets and activity schedules for Pacific blue‑economy investment programmes.
  • Manage day‑to‑day implementation of activities, including stakeholder engagement, technical assistance delivery, pipeline development and progress monitoring.
  • Manage project documentation, track financial delivery, oversee audits when required, and support organization of steering committee meetings.
  • Ensure effective coordination between countries, regional teams, and corporate oversight units to deliver a complex multi-country programme.
  • Apply UNCDF Social and Environmental Standards (SES), including safeguards related to human rights, gender equality, SEA/SH prevention, and grievance mechanisms.
  • Maintain and update project risk registers, escalate high-risk issues, and contribute to assurance activities, audits, and evaluations.
  • Apply adaptive management approaches, identifying implementation risks and bottlenecks and proposing timely corrective actions.
  • Ensure efficient use of project resources, value for money, and adherence to approved budgets.

2) Investment Pipeline Development and Blended Finance Execution

  • Lead the sourcing, screening, and development of a diversified pipeline of blue and green economy MSMEs
  • Oversee incubation and acceleration pathways, ensuring MSMEs receive tailored technical assistance and progress toward investment readiness.
  • Guide and quality-assure financial, technical, environmental and social (ESG), and gender-lens due diligence processes for MSMEs and financial-sector partners.
  • Coordinate the structuring and deployment of investment grants, concessional loans, and credit guarantees benefiting the blue economy in line with UNCDF investment policies and approval committees.
  • Support engagement with local financial institutions, development banks, and impact investors to crowd in private capital in support of the blue economy.
  • Ensure supported enterprises are prepared for graduation to concessional or commercial finance.

  • Contribute to the design, feasibility assessment, and investor engagement for the expansion of blended finance in the blue economy, ensuring alignment with UNCDF’s catalytic mandate.

     

3) Partnership Development, Stakeholder Engagement, and Policy Dialogue

  • Serve as UNCDF’s primary focal point for blue economy related engagement with governments, central banks, regulators, donors, financial institutions, NGOs, business development service providers, and private investors.
  • Build and sustain strategic partnerships that enhance MSME incubation, financial sector capacity, and capital mobilization for blue and green economy investments.
  • Support structured dialogue with policymakers and regulators to strengthen enabling environments for sustainable finance and MSME access to capital.
  • Coordinate engagement with regional and international partners working in the blue economy to leverage synergies and avoid duplication.
  • Represent UNCDF in national, regional, and international forums related to blended finance, blue economy, and climate finance.
  • Promote South–South and Triangular Cooperation initiatives and knowledge exchange around blue economy matters.

4) Monitoring, Reporting, Knowledge Management, and Learning

  • Oversee and maintain robust M&E systems capturing both programme and investment‑level results, including blue‑economy‑specific indicators (e.g., sustainable fisheries outcomes, marine ecosystem co‑benefits, climate resilience).
  • Ensure high-quality data collection, analysis, and reporting, including disaggregation by sex, youth, sector, and country.
  • Contribute to timely and accurate donor reports, annual progress reviews, and mid-term and final evaluations.
  • Lead knowledge capture and dissemination, including case studies, lessons learned, and good practices for blue and green economy finance.
  • Support learning and replication by sharing evidence and insights within UNCDF and with regional and global partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. 

Competencies

Core Competencies - UNDP Core Competencies can be found here.

  • Achieve Results - LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact  
  • Think Innovatively - LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems
  • Learn Continuously - LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences  
  • Adapt with Agility - LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands  
  • Act with Determination - LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results  
  • Engage and Partner - LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration  
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion - LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity  

 

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Thematic Area   Name   Definition  
Business Direction & Strategy   Strategic Thinking   Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNCDF’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight. 

Business  

Development   

 Knowledge Generation   Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations. 

Business  

Management  

 Communication   Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels. 

Business  

Management   

Working with  

Evidence and Data  

 Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making  
Finance   Development finance expertise   Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.  
Business Direction & Strategy   Systems  Thinking   Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system  
Partnerships management   Private Sector engagement   Ability to identify, conduct outreach and manage relationships with the private sector. 

 

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

  • An Advanced (Master’s level) university degree in business administration, finance, marketing, economics, accounting or related fields is required.  
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

  • A minimum of 7 years (with a Masters’ Degree) or 9 years (with Bachelor’s Degree) of relevant work experience in either the financial sector or the private sector or a mix, preferably with investment and/or business management expertise. 
  • A minimum of 5 years investment experience in the blue economy and financial instruments is required.
  • Experience working in venture capital and/or banking within an international financial environment, preferably in development finance institution, impact investor or similar is required;  
  • Experience in private credit and/or equity for investments with a social mission in emerging/frontier markets, is required.  
  • Experience in project preparation and/or in development of investment opportunities, especially for investment projects focusing on blue economy in developing countries is required.  
  • Competency with financial modeling and analysis in Microsoft excel is required.  
  • Computer literacy, including proficient use of research applications is required.  

Desired Experience:

  • Experience in nature-related or climate-aligned investments  
  • Experience in evaluating environmental impacts alongside commercial viability.  
  • Understanding of  the investment needs of enterprises and the mix of debt/equity required at different growth stages—from incubation to scaling up to commercial viability.  
  • Strong knowledge of financial markets and financing for sustainable development, with the ability to apply it to strategic and/or practical situations.    
  • Strong analytical writing skills; experienced in producing concise, executive level reports (PowerPoint) and presentations, training modules and materials.  
  • A minimum of 2 years of experience in working for/in the UN System or similar international development finance institution; 

Language:

  • Written and spoken fluency in English is required;  

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination. 

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles. 

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement.  We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Within UNCDF’s thematic area of peace and resilience financing, the Pro-Congo project, a joint initiative by UNEP and UNCDF under the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI) Private Sector Window, aims to support entrepreneurs and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Congo Basin countries by providing technical assistance and access to financial instruments including grants and loans, to promote tropical forest conservation, emission reductions, job creation, and biodiversity protection. Targeting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Republic of Congo (RoC), Cameroon and Gabon, the project seeks to drive sustainable economic growth by facilitating access to capacity building, finance and market access for both mature and early-stage businesses.

To facilitate the achievement of these objectives, UNCDF seeks to hire a Project Manager to lead project implementation, coordinate the project team, and ensure successful achievement of project objectives

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Manager will report to UNCDF’s Senior Portfolio Manager and will maintain a close collaboration with the Resident Coordinator’s Office in the countries of implementation through the UNCDF Regional Lead for West and Central Africa and the Caribbean. 

Under the guidance of UNCDF’s Senior Portfolio Manager, the overall responsibility of the Project Manager will be to act as liaison for all project stakeholders, providing technical assistance and ensuring proper implementation of the Pro-Congo project. He/She will conduct the following tasks:

a)    Ensure the implementation of all project activities and achievement of deliverables:

•    Develop detailed annual workplans and timelines for all project activities, ensuring alignment with the overall project objectives and oversee effective execution.
•    Lead the overall management and timely implementation of the project outputs and activities.
•    Provide strategic guidance and management oversight to ensure project implementation is on track to ensure achievement of the planned results.
•    Lead and coordinate high-level task forces and steering committees related to the implementation of the project, including ensuring regular communication and collaboration with CAFI and UNEP for successful programme implementation.
•    Facilitate and support the work of the programme’s implementing partners and deliver specialized technical assistance for effective program implementation.
•    Ensure implementation of gender mainstreaming in line with UNDP and UNCDF guidelines and global standards. 

b)    Ensure proper monitoring and reporting of the programme:

•    Organize regular coordination meetings and draft regular progress reports as agreed in the project document, including regular briefing to donors and other relevant partners.
•    Ensure the guidelines, frameworks and requirements of CAFI are followed throughout project implementation.
•    Update the Quantum and Quantum+ Project Management tools as required and monitor changes in the external environment and promptly propose to the UNCDF management of necessary solutions/actions.
•    Monitor project progress, Environmental & Social Safeguards, and risks, ensuring that changes are controlled and problems addressed.
•    Monitor the utilization of programme resources and budget to ensure cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
•    Take lead on the preparation of reviews and evaluations as defined in the project document.
•    Participate in the mobilization of additional resources including from CAFI. 
•    Travel to the project's target countries as needed for stakeholder engagement and on-site verification of results.

c)    Build partnerships with relevant stakeholders and undertake advocacy activities:

•    Coordinate dialogue, engagement and partnerships with the respective Government authorities and lead advocacy activities with other relevant stakeholders at both project and country level, including with bilateral, multilateral and private sector actors. 
•    Ensure alignment of the project with relevant UN initiatives in the countries/region.
•    Advise on the contribution of the project to the countries national priorities, progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and UNCDF’s Strategic Framework.

d)    Implement knowledge management activities:

•    Ensure implementation of knowledge management activities.
•    Participate in training events, communities of practice, codifying and sharing knowledge on sustainable practices.
•    Facilitate development of success stories and other communication materials. 


e)    Support broader UNCDF operations:

•    Contribute to knowledge-sharing initiatives and best practices in peace and resilience finance.
•    Share knowledge and lessons learned from private sector operations and best practices in relevant fields.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. 

Competencies

Core Competencies


Achieve Results:
LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively:
LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously:
LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility:
LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination:
LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner:
LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:
LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management:
LEVEL 3: Appropriately involves team in different stages of work and decision-making

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Thematic Area Name Definition

Partnership management Relationship management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding
Partnership management CSO engagement Knowledge and understanding of CSOs and the ability to engage with CSOs
Partnership management Strategic engagement Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives
Business Direction & Strategy Strategic Thinking Ability to develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNCDF’s objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, potential risks and opportunities; linking the vision to reality on the ground, and creating tangible solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight
Business Direction & Strategy Entrepreneurial Thinking Identify and seize opportunities to service and add value to clients, create clarity around UNCDF value proposition to beneficiaries and partners, develop clear service offers responding to client needs in line with UNCDF’s organizational priorities and mandate.
Business Direction & Strategy System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system
Business Management Portfolio Management Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimising return on investment. . Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Environmental Sciences, Development Studies, International Relations, Programme or Project Management, Economics, or related fields is required, or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in above or related fields in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master´s degree.

Experience:

Minimum 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant work experience in managing complex, multi-country projects or programmes in climate, environment, sustainable finance or international development, including work planning, resource and budget monitoring, results-based management and risk management.

Required Skills:

International experience working in developing countries in Africa.  
Track record of experience managing donor-funded projects (CAFI, UNCDF, UN agencies, or similar).

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

Experience with reporting to and managing donor and partner relationships including grants and reporting mechanisms. 
Experience applying UNDP and UNCDF rules, procedures, and corporate project-management tools
Experience leading a multidisciplinary project or programme team, including non-staff personnel, consultants or implementing partners.
Experience working with the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI), Global Funds, IFIs, UNCDF and/or another UN entity. 
Experience of engaging with private sector, development partners and government stakeholders in Central Africa.
Experience managing or overseeing private-sector investment programmes and/or transactions, including investment due diligence, transaction structuring and/or monitoring of financing instruments for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).

Required Languages:

Fluency in French and English, is required.  
Working knowledge of another United Nations official language is an asset.

Travel and Reimbursement:

The Project Manager is expected to render services from the UNCDF regional office in Dakar, Senegal. UNCDF will cover the cost of travel of the individual to the duty station, as well as their return to their home upon completion of their services. Frequent travel within Central Africa (DRC, RoC, Gabon and Cameroon) for stakeholder engagement and on-site verification of project activities will be required and will be paid for by UNCDF, in accordance with UNCDF travel policies. A separate TOR with clear deliverables, budget and timelines will be prepared and agreed prior to each field mission.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination. 

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles. 

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement.  We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Associate Programme Management Officer, P2
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is the leading global environmental authority that sets the global environmental agenda, promotes the coherent implementation of the environmental dimension of sustainable development within the United Nations system and serves as an authoritative advocate for the global environment. UNEP’s Ecosystem Division drives conservation, restoration and sustainable use of ecosystems to achieve benefits for nature and people: today and future generations. The division works with Member States and partners to strengthen resilience by providing policy and technical support to catalyze sustainable social and economic transformation for biodiversity, people and peace. The Associate Programme Management Officer will operate in the framework of the "Resilient Mountains” project including its “Adaptation at Altitude" and “MountainsAdapt” components and other related activities focusing on the nexus between nature and climate action in mountain ecosystems and will contribute in providing assistance in support of the implementation of the aforementioned project (components) and related activities with a particular focus on the South Caucasus region and other mountain ecosystems across the world, also closely liaising with UNEP´s relevant Divisions, Regional Office for Europe and its Vienna Programme office as well as other partners within the UN system. “Adaptation at Altitude” project (component) The overall objective of the Adaptation at Altitude (A@A) programme (led by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation) is to increase understanding on how the climate–land-use interactions are impacting tropical mountain biodiversity and ecosystem functions and appropriate conservation, restoration, sustainable use, adaptation and nature-based solutions in mountains and feed it into science-policy platforms for informed decision-making in national, regional and global policy processes, to increase the resilience and adaptive capacity of mountain communities and ecosystems to land uses and climate change. UNEP has been selected to lead the work under Outcome 2 to support regional policy action in the South Caucasus and East Africa as well as the interregional level. Strengthening South-South and regional cooperation and concrete action is furthermore seen as an effective catalyzer for adequate policy integration of mountain adaptation at national levels. “Mt Adapt” project (component) Further complementing the work on adaptation in mountain areas, the Austrian Federal Ministry for Climate Action decided to support the MountainsADAPT project, coordinated by UNEP, with the aim that innovative mountain adaptation nature-based solutions are widely known among targeted stakeholders and are implemented through a newly established small grants funding scheme to support needs-based and context-specific adaptation financing. Following the successful first phase, a small grants funding scheme for flexible and easily accessible financing of mountain adaptation solutions is rolled-out further supported by targeted capacity-building and training measures. This post is located in the Biodiversity, People and Landscapes Unit in the Biodiversity and Land Branch (BLB), Ecosystems Division, at the Vienna duty station (hosted at Vienna Programme Office). Under overall direction of Branch and Unit Head and direct supervision of the Mountain Team Leader, the incumbent will be responsible for the following duties: Responsibilities • Works with key partners and stakeholders and provides technical and administrative support to the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the assigned project (components); monitors and analyzes specific aspects of project development and implementation; reviews relevant documents and reports; identifies problems and issues to be addressed and recommends corrective actions; liaises with relevant parties; identifies and tracks follow-up actions. • Assists in defining and establishing synergies and cooperation in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals, the Medium-Term Strategy and the Kunming Montreal-Global Biodiversity Framework, connecting with other activities and initiatives in the assigned thematic fields, closely working with relevant thematic units and wider UNEP network; supporting the development of initiatives and project ideas, including targeted resource mobilization, targeting both horizontal and vertical funding. • Carries out basic research on selected thematic aspects, operations and other activities, related to mountain ecosystems and climate change, including collecting, analyzing and presenting statistical data and other information gathered from diverse sources. • Provides substantive support for policy coordination and evaluation functions, including the review and analysis of emerging development issues and trends in ecosystem degradation, biodiversity loss and climate change in in tropical mountain ecosystems. • Assists in performing consulting assignments, in collaboration with partners, by planning facilitating workshops, through other interactive sessions and assisting in developing the action plan the client will use to manage the change. • Contributes to the preparation of various written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analytical notes, sections of reports and studies, inputs to publications that relate to mountain ecosystems • Provides administrative and substantive support to consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying and proposed participants, preparation of background documents and presentations, handling logistics, etc. • Undertakes outreach activities related to the global mountains programme, assigned project (components) and topics; participates in the development of training workshops, seminars, etc.; participates in and makes presentations on assigned topics/activities. • Participates in field missions, including provision of substantive and administrative support, data collection, etc. • Coordinates activities related to budget funding (project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and preparation of related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, project budget, etc.). • Contributes to the collection and analysis of data as well as identification of trends or patterns and provides draft insights through graphs, charts, tables and reports using data visualization methods for data-driven planning, decision-making, presentation and reporting • Performs other duties as required. Competencies • PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge and understanding of concepts and approach relevant to project development and implementation, review of relevant documents, reports and research. Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to develop sources for data collection. Ability to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. •TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • PLANNING AND ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree, equivalent or higher) in a field relevant to mountains, ecosystem management, biodiversity conservation, and restoration, climate change adaptation, regional governance, including environmental sciences, sustainable development or a related field. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Successful completion of both degree and non-degree programs in data analytics, business analytics or data science programs is desirable. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of two (2) years of progressively responsible experience in project management, including experience in biodiversity conservation and/or ecosystem-based adaptation is required Work experience in policy mainstreaming and advocacy is required. Working experience in sustainable mountain development, including in the (South) Caucasus region, is required. Working experience with the set-up of small-grants mechanism, benefiting mainly Community Based Organizations (CBOs), is desirable. Experience in developing tools, methodologies, and guidance, preferably with a focus on nature aspects of climate change adaptation is desirable. A minimum of one (1) year of more experience in data analytics or related area is desirable (none if successful YPP or P-1 with a related degree) Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). Required Languages Language Reading Writing Listening Speaking English UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II UN Level II Assessment Evaluation of qualified candidates may include an assessment exercise which may be followed by competency-based interview. Special Notice The appointment against this position is limited to the United Nations Environment Programme. Appointment against this position is for an initial period of one (1) year and may be subject to extension. External candidate selected for this position will be granted a fixed-term appointment limited ("FTA-limited") in accordance with section 2.2 (b) of administrative instruction ST/AI/2013/1 on Administration of fixed-term appointments. Renewal of appointment is contingent upon continued existence of mandate and availability of funding. If this position is discontinued, the incumbent will be separated from service. United Nations Secretariat staff members who meet the definition of "internal candidate" in staff rule 4.10 who are selected for this position subject to limitation will retain their current appointment status and will be reassigned or transferred to the position, without a lien to their parent position. Pursuant to section 7.11 of ST/AI/2012/2/Rev.1, candidates recruited through the young professionals' programme who have not served for a minimum of two years in the position of their initial assignment are not eligible to apply to this position. Staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General and to assignment by him or her. In this context, all staff are expected to move periodically to new functions in their careers in accordance with established rules and procedures. The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance and geographical diversity in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. When completing the Candidate Profile form, ensure ALL fields, ALL professional experience and contact information are completed and up to date. This information is the basis for the hiring manager to assess your eligibility and suitability for the position and to contact you. Individual Contractors and Consultants who have worked within the UN Secretariat in the last six months, are ineligible to apply for or be appointed to any professional and higher temporary or fixed-term positions, within six months of the end of their current or most recent service. For such positions, at least six months need to have elapsed between the end of a consultancy or individual contract and the time of application and consideration for an appointment as a staff member under the Staff Rules and Regulations of the United Nations. The requirement is not applicable when a person considered for appointment is serving or has previously served as affiliated personnel (for example as a consultant, individual contractor, intern or gratis personnel) with a specialized agency or an Office, Fund or Programme such as UNHCR, UNICEF, UNDP or UNOPS which is separately administered and funded from voluntary contributions At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application. On-line applications will be acknowledged where an email address has been provided. All applicants are strongly encouraged to apply on-line as soon as possible after the job opening has been posted and well before the deadline stated in the job opening. If you do not receive an e-mail acknowledgement within 24 hours of submission, your application may not have been received. If the problem persists, please seek technical assistance through the Inspira "Contact Us" link. United Nations Considerations According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions. Applicants are urged to carefully follow all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira, and to refer to the Applicant Guide by clicking on “Manuals” in the “Help” tile of the inspira account-holder homepage. The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines. Applicants must provide complete and accurate information pertaining to their personal profile and qualifications according to the instructions provided in inspira to be considered for the current job opening. No amendment, addition, deletion, revision or modification shall be made to applications that have been submitted. Candidates under serious consideration for selection will be subject to reference checks to verify the information provided in the application. All external candidates recruited in accordance with section ‎2.2 (a) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment without limitation and all external candidates recruited in accordance with section 2.2. (c) of ST/AI/2025/3 for a fixed term appointment limited to the entity are subject to an initial probationary period of one year under a fixed-term appointment. Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date. No Fee THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.
